sections.section_title: Atypical Presentation and Initial Differential: Neck Swelling Beyond Angioedema
sections.description: Covers the patient’s presenting features, early impressions (Ludwig’s angina and idiopathic angioedema), and how focused history and exam redirected the differential toward dermatomyositis.
subtopics: Presenting complaints: progressive neck swelling, proximal hip-flexor weakness, mild myalgia, dysphagia signals (coughing/increased secretions on nasendoscopy)
Red flags against angioedema: afebrile, no ACEi/NSAID/DPP-4 use, no urticaria, normal C4/C1-INH studies, persistent non-tender edema, violaceous facial erythema including nasolabial folds
ENT and infectious differentials: Ludwig’s angina, deep neck space infection, cellulitis/erysipelas, sialadenitis; role of CT neck showing diffuse strap muscle edema without abscess

Neuromuscular/inflammatory differentials: idiopathic inflammatory myopathies, immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy, inclusion body myositis, myasthenia gravis; delayed drug reactions; orofacial granulomatosis; hypocomplementemic urticarial vasculitis; SVC syndrome
Key bedside clues to dermatomyositis: periungual erythema and capillary microhemorrhages, Holster sign on thigh, proximal weakness, dysphagia
Early pivot test: ordering creatine kinase (very high at 16,184 U/L) to distinguish myositis-related edema from angioedema

sections.section_title: Pathobiology of Dermatomyositis and the SAE1 Phenotype
sections.description: Explains the immunopathogenesis of dermatomyositis, mechanisms for pseudoangioedema and dysphagia, and the clinical phenotype associated with anti-SAE1 autoantibodies.
subtopics: Dermatomyositis overview: complement-mediated microangiopathy, perifascicular ischemia and atrophy, and capillary C5b-9 deposition
Mechanism of ‘pseudoangioedema’: inflammatory myofasciitis and subcutaneous tissue edema from muscle inflammation rather than histamine/bradykinin pathways
Oropharyngeal involvement: cricopharyngeal and pharyngeal muscle weakness causing dysphagia, aspiration risk, and extrathoracic restrictive pattern on PFTs
SUMOylation pathway and SAE1: biology of SUMO-activating enzyme; relevance of anti-SAE1 antibodies to cutaneous prominence (heliotrope, shawl/V signs), dysphagia, and ILD risk
Comparative serology context: how SAE1 differs from Mi-2, TIF1-γ, MDA5, antisynthetase (e.g., Jo-1) with respect to skin, lung, malignancy associations
Epidemiology highlights: adult-onset peak, rarity of generalized edema; why neck/facial swelling may trigger ENT/angioedema pathways

sections.section_title: Diagnostic Workup and Reasoning: From Enceinte Neck Edema to Dermatomyositis
sections.description: Details the targeted investigations and how each contributed to confirming dermatomyositis and excluding mimics, including malignancy workup and organ involvement screening.
subtopics: Key labs: markedly elevated CK; AST/ALT/LDH pattern consistent with muscle injury; normal renal function and negative urine myoglobin
Angioedema assessment: normal C3/C4, normal C1-INH function/level excluding bradykinin-mediated angioedema
Autoimmunity testing: high-titer speckled ANA; myositis panel strongly positive for anti-SAE1; negative Mi-2, TIF1-γ, Jo-1, OJ; infection screen prior to immunosuppression
Imaging for myositis: MRI thighs with active myositis in pelvic/hip muscles; FDG-PET showing diffuse skeletal muscle uptake predominantly head/neck, shoulders, trunk

Swallowing and pulmonary evaluation: videofluoroscopic evidence of severe pharyngeal dysphagia with penetration; CT chest showing aspiration changes and non-cavitating nodules; PFTs with extrathoracic restrictive pattern; absence of ILD on CT
Histopathology: perifascicular necrosis/degeneration/regeneration, perimysial inflammation with histiocytes, capillary C5b-9 deposition diagnostic of dermatomyositis

Malignancy risk stratification (IMACS): high-risk categorization (dermatomyositis + dysphagia; intermediate factors male sex, SAE1+); negative baseline CT chest/abdomen/pelvis, PET, tumor markers; plan for GI endoscopies and interval surveillance
Synthesis: converging evidence for SAE1-positive dermatomyositis with prominent cervical inflammatory edema and severe dysphagia due to pharyngeal myopathy

sections.section_title: Acute and Longitudinal Management: Airway-Safe Immunosuppression and Supportive Care
sections.description: Outlines immediate stabilization, immunomodulatory regimen selection and sequencing, rationale for agent choice/avoidance, prophylaxis, and dysphagia/nutrition strategies.
subtopics: Airway and aspiration management: ENT monitoring, early recognition of pharyngeal weakness, NG tube feeding to protect airway and maintain nutrition
Induction therapy: IV methylprednisolone 1 g daily for 3 days for severe muscle/airway involvement; transition to oral prednisone taper starting at 60 mg
Steroid-sparing and adjuncts: IVIG loading (2 g/kg) followed by monthly cycles; mycophenolate mofetil (1 g BID) as first-line steroid-sparing agent; rituximab 1 g x2 two weeks apart in severe disease
Agent selection rationale: avoidance of methotrexate given abnormal lung function/ILD risk; azathioprine/tacrolimus reserved as alternatives due to good MMF tolerance
Infection prophylaxis and safety: PJP prophylaxis selection (TMP-SMX intolerance → monthly inhaled pentamidine), vaccination considerations (VZV IgG negative), latent TB evaluation complexities
Rehabilitation and monitoring: swallow therapy, aspiration precautions, physical therapy for proximal weakness, CK/LFT monitoring, glucose/BP/bone protection on steroids
Escalation/adjustment strategy: criteria to taper steroids, continue IVIG, de-escalate MMF; indications for reconsidering agents if relapse or ILD/malignancy emerges

sections.section_title: Outcomes, Follow-up, and Prognosis in SAE1-Positive Dermatomyositis
sections.description: Summarizes clinical trajectory, objective response measures, long-term surveillance, and expected prognosis with emphasis on dysphagia recovery and malignancy monitoring.
subtopics: Clinical response timeline: early reduction in neck edema; CK normalization by 3 weeks; full proximal strength recovery by 3 weeks; NG removal at 2 months; complete resolution of cervical edema by 3 months; steroid cessation by 7 months
Pulmonary course: improving restrictive pattern; near-complete resolution of aspiration-related opacities by 11 months; stable exercise tolerance at 12 months
Functional recovery: return to oral intake, physical endurance, and ADLs
Long-term immunosuppression plan: continuation of IVIG with planned MMF taper; individualized weaning based on symptoms, CK, and strength
Malignancy surveillance: symptom review, exam, labs, serial chest imaging, scheduled endoscopies; counseling on ongoing risk despite negative baseline screen
Prognostic considerations: generally favorable outcome with prompt, aggressive therapy; recognition that prominent edema can portend severe disease but is reversible with treatment

sections.section_title: Key Clinical Lessons and Decision Algorithms
sections.description: Provides teachable points and stepwise approaches to avoid misdiagnosis and expedite care in patients with neck/facial swelling where angioedema is suspected.
subtopics: When ‘angioedema’ isn’t angioedema: persistent, non-urticarial, non-pruritic swelling with normal complement/C1-INH and subtle DM skin signs should prompt CK testing
Focused exam checklist: periungual changes, violaceous facial erythema, Holster/shawl/V signs, proximal weakness, dysphagia indicators (wet voice, cough with swallow)
Rapid workup algorithm for suspected myositis with neck edema: CK → myositis panel → MRI/PET for distribution → swallow study/PFTs → biopsy if needed
Risk stratification and screening: apply IMACS cancer-screening framework early; align immunotherapy with lung status and severity of dysphagia
Early immunosuppression saves function: prioritize high-dose steroids plus IVIG in severe pharyngeal involvement; add steroid-sparing agent promptly
Interdisciplinary care: coordinate ENT, immunology/rheumatology, neurology, speech pathology, nutrition, and pulmonology for airway safety and rehabilitation
